scenes.title: Reading the Festival Rules
scenes.summary: On Monday morning of Festival Week, F1, M2, and M4 read the official rulebook and discover every participating courtyard must display its original founding brass plaque.
scenes.intro: Bright Monday morning sunshine fills the lobby of {SHOW} in {CITY}. Five days before the Historic Courtyard Festival opens on Saturday, {F1}, {M2}, and {M4} lean over a cream rulebook delivered from City Hall. Listen first.
story: M2
Behold page one, my friends: {SHOW} is officially Courtyard Number Five on Saturday!
F1
Five historic courtyards across {CITY}, and visitors vote for the Golden Plaque!
M4
Before you start polishing your speech, {M2}, let us check the three entry rules.
F1
Rule One: safe public stone walkways and open ground-floor seating from ten until six.
M2
Check! Twenty-eight windproof seats, clean flagstones, and zero loose posters!
M4
Rule Two: live acoustic music or local neighbourhood craft demonstrations during the day.
F1
Check! {F3}, {M3}, and {F2} have music and warm pastries covered!
M2
See how easy this is, {M4}? What tiny formality is Rule Number Three?
M4
Rule Three: display your original founding brass builder plaque beside the street gate.
F1
Wait a second—do we HAVE a founding brass builder plaque beside our gate?!
M2
Of course we do! Pull down my glasses—wait, has anyone looked at the gate lately?
M4
Let us walk outside right now and inspect the limestone arch for ourselves!
scenes.outro: Rules One and Two are easy, while Rule Three sends everyone marching straight out to inspect the limestone gate! See you next time.

scenes.title: Four Empty Screw Holes
scenes.summary: Outside by the front archway, M1 points out four empty brass screw holes in the stone wall where the founding oval plaque used to hang.
scenes.intro: Stepping outside onto {STREET}, {F1} and {M2} find {M1} sweeping morning leaves beside the arched limestone entrance of {SHOW}. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
{M1}, please tell us there is an old brass builder plaque on this wall!
M1
Look right beside the bell pull at eye level—what do you two see?
M2
I see a pale oval shadow on the stone and four empty screw holes!
F1
Wait—there really WAS an oval plaque bolted right here beside the gate!
M1
When I started working here fifteen years ago, those four holes were already empty.
M2
Wait a minute... twenty years back, workmen cleaned the stone arch before painting!
F1
Did the workmen unscrew the founding brass plaque so paint would not splash it?
M1
Workmen unscrew things, boss, and owners put them somewhere safe and forget.
M2
Me, forget a historical treasure?! I have an organizational system like clockwork!
M1
Says the man currently wearing two pairs of reading glasses on one forehead.
F1
Never mind the glasses—without that oval plaque by Friday, do we lose our spot?!
M1
Start in the cellar tool chests while I check the back hallway cupboard.
scenes.outro: Four empty holes on the gate arch launch a house-wide treasure hunt with five days left before Saturday! See you next time.

scenes.title: Searching the Back Cupboard
scenes.summary: In the back hallway cupboard behind the kitchen, F2, F3, and M1 sort through brass candlesticks and curtain rings without finding the missing gate plaque.
scenes.intro: In the cool back hallway behind the café corner, {M1} unlocks the deep oak storage cupboard while {F2} wipes flour from her apron and {F3} holds a small flashlight. Listen first.
story: F2
Goodness, {M1}, how many brass objects can one eight-room guesthouse own?!
M1
Six curtain rods, four tea trays, two door knockers, and zero oval gate plaques.
F3
Hold the light toward the back corner shelf, {M1}—something metal is gleaming there!
F2
Pull it out gently, {M1}! Is it oval, heavy, and stamped with a date?!
M1
Round, light, and dented—that is my old soup kettle lid from ten winters ago.
F2
False alarm! Where else would {M2} hide something shiny during facade repairs?
F3
When careful people store an heirloom away, they usually leave a note in a ledger.
M1
My front-desk ledger only goes back fifteen years, madam, not twenty.
F3
What about that old green family guest book {M2} brought out on Saturday?
F2
Brilliant idea, {F3}! His aunt wrote down every repair and receipt in the back pages!
M1
And {M2} kept using those back pages during his first five years as owner.
F3
Let us take a pot of tea into Room Nine and read the repair pages!
scenes.outro: The hallway cupboard yields only a dented kettle lid, pointing {F3} straight toward the back pages of the old green guest book. See you next time.

scenes.title: A Receipt in Blue Ink
scenes.summary: Turning to the back of the green guest book in Room 9, M2, F3, and M3 find a metal-polishing receipt and a note in M2's own handwriting.
scenes.intro: Inside bright Room 9, {M3} stops by with his leather notebook as {M2} and {F3} flip to the repair index at the very back of the green cloth book. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M3
Any luck finding the founding date or the missing gate plaque yet, {M2}?
M2
Flip past the roof tiles and the boiler pipe, {F3}—here is Gate Arch Cleaning!
F3
Look, a narrow yellow shop ticket is pinned neatly to the corner of the page!
M3
Let me read the stamp: Old Quarter Brass and Copper Polisher, {STREET}, paid in full.
M2
Aha! Now I remember—I sent the tarnished oval plaque down the lane for polishing!
F3
Keep reading below the yellow ticket, {M2}; that blue ink looks remarkably familiar.
M2
Lent polished oval gate plaque to the {STREET} Neighbourhood History Display for two weeks!
M3
Wait—you lent it for two weeks TEN YEARS AGO and never picked it up?!
M2
In my defence, {M3}, that was a very busy spring at the front desk!
F3
Do not despair, {M2}; at least we know the plaque was polished, not lost!
M3
I walk past the old brass polisher shopfront every day—let us check after lunch!
M2
Hurry back, because someone very official just walked through our courtyard gate!
scenes.outro: A ten-year-old blue-ink note solves half the mystery, right as a crisp visitor steps through the gate! See you at the front desk next time.

scenes.title: The Rival Brochure
scenes.summary: At the front desk, F1, M2, and F2 inspect a glossy festival brochure dropped off by a courier from the three-time champion Clock-Square Courtyard.
scenes.intro: At the front desk, {F1} holds a thick gold-bordered brochure just delivered by a neighbourhood bicycle courier while {M2} and {F2} lean across the counter. Listen first.
story: M2
Was that a City Hall inspector at the door, {F1}? Did they check the gate?!
F1
Relax, {M2}—it was a courier delivering sample brochures from Courtyard Number One!
F2
Courtyard Number One? Is that the big Clock-Square Courtyard near the fountain?
F1
Yes! Look at the cover: Three-Time Winner of the {CITY} Golden Courtyard Plaque!
M2
Look at their glossy colour photographs: marble columns, velvet ropes, and brass trumpets!
F2
Velvet ropes inside a neighbourhood courtyard? Where are people supposed to drink tea?!
F1
Wait—read the festival notice printed inside the back flap of the booklet, both of you!
M2
Notice to Hosts: Three Festival Judges will visit each courtyard anonymously before Saturday!
F2
ANONYMOUSLY?! You mean any customer ordering coffee this week could be a secret judge?!
M2
Sound the alarm! Polish every spoon! Nobody slouches behind the counter until Sunday!
F1
Calm down, {M2}; last time you panicked about an inspector, it was just {M3}!
M2
This time it is printed in black ink—every stranger is a judge until proven innocent!
scenes.outro: Anonymous festival judges are roaming {CITY} all week, sending {M2} straight into five-star high alert! See you next time.

scenes.title: Closed Metal Shop
scenes.summary: Walking up {STREET} to find the old brass polisher, F1 and M3 learn at the second-hand bookshop arch that the retired craftsman donated unclaimed displays to the street archive.
scenes.intro: Early Monday afternoon on {STREET}, {F1} and {M3} pause beside the stone arch of the second-hand bookshop, two doors past a shuttered brass-polishing workshop. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
The brass polisher shop has flower boxes in the window—it is a tailor studio now!
M3
Do not give up yet, {F1}; look at the notice card inside the arch.
F1
Old Quarter History Shelf—curated from neighbourhood shops along {STREET}!
M3
Remember what {M2} wrote in the green book? He lent the plaque to a street display!
F1
Let us check the ledger tied with string beside the green lending shelf here.
M3
Flip back ten summers... Brass Shop Window Exhibit: Six Historic Door and Gate Plates!
F1
Item Number Four: Oval Brass Founding Plaque from {SHOW}, lent for summer festival!
M3
And look at the transfer stamp beside Item Four when the brass shop closed.
F1
Transferred for safekeeping to the Municipal Street Archive Case at Clock-Square Pavilion!
M3
My brother {M4} works right at City Hall—he can check who holds the key!
F1
From four empty screw holes at breakfast to an exact location after lunch!
M3
Let us call {M4} from the front desk before {M2} mistakes the postman for a judge!
scenes.outro: An old transfer stamp under the bookshop arch points straight to a locked display case at Clock-Square Pavilion! See you next time.

scenes.title: Acoustic Test One
scenes.summary: Back in the courtyard, F3 plays a bright melody inside Room 9 while M3 and M1 notice the stone archway scatters soft notes toward the street.
scenes.intro: Late Monday afternoon at {SHOW}, {F3} steps out to the courtyard doorway after playing a lively scale inside Room 9 while {M3} listens near the gate arch alongside {M1}. Listen first.
story: F3
Well, gentlemen, how clearly did that piano melody reach the front gate arch?
M3
Inside the courtyard under the shade tree, every single note sounds warm and clear.
M1
Near the stone fountain and the street arch, however, the high notes bounce around.
F3
Interesting! On Friday night we had twenty-eight seated neighbours listening in complete silence.
M3
On Festival Saturday, fifty visitors will be walking, chatting, and pouring tea at once.
M1
Bare brick along the side arcade acts like a mirror when a crowd talks.
F3
Can an acoustic architect soften a brick wall without drilling holes in historic stone, {M3}?
M3
Easily, {F3}: freestanding cedar frames wrapped in heavy natural linen soak up chatter!
M1
And direct the clean piano and violin notes straight toward the middle tables.
F3
Like invisible curtains that help the music float above the teacups!
M1
Draw me the wood measurements tonight, {M3}; I have dry cedar boards downstairs.
M3
Deal—and look, here comes {M4} through the gate with news from City Hall!
scenes.outro: A smart cedar-and-linen plan takes shape for Saturday's sound, just as {M4} arrives with news of the display-case key! See you next time.

scenes.title: Keeper of the Archive Key
scenes.summary: At the front desk, M4 reveals that the oval plaque sits safe inside the Clock-Square display case—and the retired street archivist who holds the key is out of town until Wednesday morning!
scenes.intro: At the front desk as evening lamps click on, {M4} opens his City Hall folder before {F1} and {M2}. Listen to the final scene of Episode 1 first.
story: M2
Tell me good news, {M4}—did you rescue our founding brass plaque from City Hall?!
M4
Better than a guess, {M2}: I saw your oval brass plaque through the pavilion glass myself!
F1
YES! What is engraved on the front—could you read it through the glass?!
M4
Only the top border because an old velvet ribbon covers the lower half inside.
M2
Why did you not unlock the wooden case and carry it straight down {STREET}?
M4
Because the Neighbourhood History Society holds the only brass key to that cabinet!
F1
Who is the secretary of the Neighbourhood History Society on {STREET}, {M4}?
M4
You already know him well: the retired violinist next door at house number ten!
M2
Our violinist friend from Friday night holds the key?! Let us knock on his door!
M4
One tiny catch: his sister said he took the bus to visit family until Wednesday!
F1
Wednesday morning—AND meanwhile three secret judges could walk through our gate tomorrow!
M2
Everyone iron your collars tonight: Tuesday morning, operation Five-Star Welcome begins!
scenes.outro: The oval plaque sits behind glass until Wednesday morning—while Tuesday brings {M2}'s hilarious hunt for secret festival judges! End of Episode 1—see you in Episode 2!
